capitals.note: The page names Riga the capital, the second-largest city of the Swedish Empire; ruled by governors-general (Jacob De la Gardie 1622-1628, Erik Dahlberg 1696-1702) but with its own diet.

ledger.note: August 1621: the Swedish invasion of Livonia begins; the siege of Riga opened on 29 August.

region.text: Riga and the fortress of Daugavgriva (Dünamünde)

ledger.note: 25 September 1621: Riga capitulates to Gustavus Adolphus and Swedish Livonia begins. 'Riga capitulated on 25 September' after three assaults; Dünamünde (Daugavgriva) fell on 2 October 1621.

ledger.note: January 1622: Valmiera (Wolmar) and several smaller Livonian castles fall to the Swedes.
1625: Koknese falls after a sixteen-day siege (the Swedes landed in June 1625).
27 August 1625: Dorpat (Tartu) falls to the Swedes.

ledger.note: 25 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark recognises Sweden's conquest of most of the Duchy of Livonia. The page: 'Sweden took most of the Polish-Lithuanian Duchy of Livonia'; the year is the page's, the extent (the rest of Vidzeme and southern Estonia) is the researcher's reading, since the 1621 page dates only Riga, Valmiera, Dorpat and Koknese.

region.text: Livonia north of Latgale without Ösel: Vidzeme, Riga and southern Estonia

ledger.note: 25 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark ends the fighting for Livonia; the Commonwealth keeps the Inflanty Voivodeship.

13 August 1645: the Treaty of Brömsebro gives Sweden the island of Ösel. 'Denmark-Norway ceded this Danish Baltic Sea island to Sweden' (with Gotland, Halland for thirty years, Jämtland and Härjedalen). Denmark-Norway's own dossier files the loss under the counterpart swedish-empire.

23 April 1660: the Treaty of Oliva formally cedes Livonia to Sweden; the page: 'the whole territory was formally ceded'. No land changes hands in 1660; the province had been Swedish since 1629 and Poland had only a truce until then.

March 1700: Augustus II's Saxon forces invade Swedish Livonia and besiege Riga. 'Augustus II's forces advanced through Swedish Livonia, captured Dünamünde, and laid siege to Riga' (the page gives the siege no end month).
June 1701: Charles XII defeats the Saxons and Russians at the Düna crossing and then Augustus at Riga; the siege is over.

region.text: Livonia north of Latgale: Vidzeme, Riga and the Dorpat and Fellin districts

ledger.note: 4/15 July 1710: Riga and the Livonian nobility capitulate to Russia. 'The Livonian nobility and the city of Riga capitulated on 4 July 1710 (O.S.) / 15 July 1710 (N.S.)'; the capitulations confirmed the Baltic German privileges and the Protestant church order. The page does not say when Dorpat fell (it names no 1704 capture).
August 1710: Pernau (Pärnu) capitulates. 'Pernau (Pärnu): capitulated in August 1710.'

1710: Ösel passes to Russia with the rest of Livonia. Page silent: the capitulation page names Ösel only as a planned Swedish naval assault of 1711 that never took place, and the Swedish Livonia page says 'following the Capitulation of Estonia and Livonia' the whole territory formed Riga Governorate; the month is bridging.

1710: Swedish rule in Livonia ends. 'Following the Capitulation of Estonia and Livonia' the territory 'formed Riga Governorate under Russian control'; the Treaty of Nystad (30 August 1721) gave Russia Livonia, Estonia and Ingria formally (Great Northern War page).

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1621-1625)

union.text: Valmiera (Wolmar) and the smaller castles taken in January 1622

wars.outcome: Sweden took Riga (25 September 1621), Valmiera (January 1622), Koknese and Dorpat (1625) and kept Livonia north of the Daugava; the Truce of Altmark (25 September 1629) recognised the gains.
wars.note: Truces of Mitau 10 August 1622 and, on the page's intro, November 1622.

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Brömsebro, 13 August 1645: Denmark-Norway ceded Ösel and Gotland, Jämtland and Härjedalen, and Halland for thirty years.
wars.note: The page names the Torstenson War as the war the treaty ended; the war's course is not on the page.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Russia captured Riga and Tallinn in 1710 and 'evicted Sweden from the Baltic provinces'; the Treaty of Nystad (30 August 1721 O.S.) gave Russia Estonia, Livonia, Ingria and Kexholm.
wars.note: Saxon siege of Riga March 1700; Charles XII at the Düna June 1701.

certainty.note: Shapes follow modern county and commune names; the Latgale (Inflanty) line of 1629 is the truce line but the page names only the region. Sharp would need the Altmark boundary.

notes: Type colony: Swedish Livonia was a province of the Swedish crown with its own diet, not a separate sovereign; Cliopatria draws the land inside its Swedish Empire shapes (1629-1712), so the renderer should draw it as a tint of Sweden, not a rival colour. Five pages opened (within 2-5). Not settled: the dates of Dorpat's and Fellin's fall to Sweden after 1625 (pages silent), the fall of Dorpat to Russia (1704 is not on any opened page), the date Ösel passed to Russia in 1710, the Livonian-Polish boundary of 1629 (Latgale used as a stand-in; Inflanty is Latgale on the page). Counterpart 'denmark-norway' for Ösel: that dossier files its 1645 loss under 'swedish-empire'. The Treaty of Oliva (23 April 1660) is a rename event only because no land moved. Kokenhusen, Fellin and Wenden named in the 1600-1611 war are in the duchy-of-livonia dossier. Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): the region {admin1: Riga, country: Latvia} resolved to the whole Riga planning region (30 municipalities, about 13,150 km2), not the city; replaced by a circle round the city (10 km: Riga with Daugavgriva/Dünamünde).
